title: MANGAL (the season key art)
caption:
Rukawat ke liye khed hai. We were away for eleven weeks.

In Marathi, Hindi, Gujarati, Bengali and more, Tuesday is named for Mangal, and mangal also means auspicious. So the season has one name, and the posts carry it from one language to the next. Find yours.

First piece: the Baguette Tennis Bracelet in Ruby, ₹1,699. It pairs with the Ruby Baguette Huggies, ₹1,199. Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. Your bag applies the code, BUY2 or BUY3, by itself.

Today's mangal: all of them.

[ baguette tennis bracelet · 18k gold tone plated · no muhurat needed ]
first_comment: Which script did you read first? Free insured shipping. Cash on delivery available. #NairaFlore #NairaPetite #DemiFineJewellery #TennisBracelet #EditionTwo
alt_text: Slide 1: on a soft blush ground, the word MANGAL in large dark red capitals with a thin orange print edge, and under it one quiet line with the same word in Marathi, Hindi and Gujarati scripts. Below lies a real bracelet of ruby-red rectangular stones in gold-tone claws. A line at the foot reads Tuesday, and every auspicious day. The NAIRA wordmark sits top left.

Slide 2: a dictionary page on ivory headed MANGAL, TWO WAYS, with the line it means auspicious; in most of these languages, it is also Tuesday. A ruled table sets the word for mangal in Marathi, Hindi, Gujarati, Bengali, Kannada, Telugu, Punjabi, Urdu, Tamil and Malayalam beside each language's word for Tuesday, with the shared mangal part in dark red and the rest in grey; Tamil and Malayalam give Tuesday its own name. It closes: so this season, we stopped waiting for a muhurat.

Slide 3: on blush, the words No muhurat needed above a close-up photograph of ruby-red baguette stones in gold-tone claws. Below it: ruby-red cubic zirconia, on an ordinary Tuesday. Baguette Tennis Bracelet, Ruby, 1,699 rupees. 18K gold tone plated. At the foot, the NAIRA and MANGAL seal with the Marathi word मंगळ and a small steel key.

Caption: 'every post carries it in a different script' changed to 'the posts carry it from one language to the next'. Marathi and Hindi share one script (Devanagari), P1 itself sets two Devanagari words, and P3 and P12 repeat Marathi, so 'a different script' each post was not true; consecutive posts do change language.

Caption line 1: 'Rukawat ke liye khed hai.' (spec 'Rukavat'): Rukawat is the transliteration the Doordarshan card is remembered and searched by, and recognition is the whole point of the opening line.

Caption offer sentence: 'Take 2 pieces for 10% off or 3 for 20% off. Your bag applies the code, BUY2 or BUY3, by itself.' replaces the spec's 'with codes BUY2 and BUY3 at checkout'. The bag applies the ladder and the shopper never types it (brand bible section 6; CLAUDE.md: 'The ladder is applied by the bag, never typed'), the old line told people to type codes at checkout, and 'codes BUY2 and BUY3' could read as two codes stacked when Fastrr carries exactly one. The identical sentence is in the post.json captions of P3, P4, P6, P9 and P11 (both P11 captions); P12's builder must use it too.
